key_insight: The paper argues that safety-critical autonomous systems need deterministic, enforceable coordination in hardware, while keeping higher-level semantic reasoning adaptive in software.
engineering_relevance: By mapping selected TB-CSPN coordination semantics onto FPGA primitives, the approach aims to provide bounded latency, temporal synchronization, authorization control, and safer real-time orchestration across heterogeneous AI components.
method: Use the Topic-Based Communication Space Petri Net (TB-CSPN) framework to separate semantic reasoning from interaction management.
Implement selected coordination mechanisms directly in FPGA hardware as a hardware-native semantic coordination layer.
Keep reasoning layers software-driven while hardware enforces coordination constraints such as gating, synchronization, and bounded behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual architecture and motivation; it does not report experimental results, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: A key concern is whether the FPGA-mapped coordination semantics can scale and be maintained across diverse autonomous components without introducing integration complexity or limiting flexibility.
paper_title: Hardware-Enforced Semantic Coordination for Safety-Critical Real-Time Autonomous Systems
